newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada may give relief for weather damage to crops.
newsitem.headline: Canada may give relief for weather damage to crops.

text.p: The Canadian government may extend relief to its farmers if adverse weather cuts into the harvest too much, Farm Minister Ralph Goodale said on Monday.

"The weather conditions over the last couple of weeks at least in some parts of the prairies are most definitely a matter of concern to many farmers," Goodale told Parliament in answer to a question from a left-wing member of Parliament.

"Naturally the government of Canada is concerned. We're watching the situation closely. We have of course a rather elaborate safety net system already in place to deal with producting and marketing problems that affect agriculture from time to time."
Goodale added: "And we do of course if necessary have the special provisions for special advances under government legislation which we would consider invoking if that should become necessary."
In the last two weeks the prairies have seen significant rain and snow as well as overnight frost. Half of Alberta and Saskatchewan's crops were still standing as of a week ago.
